name: Town Center & Harbour
tagline: Whitewashed lanes, the marina, and the Lycian rock tomb overhead
description: The historic heart of Kas, all whitewashed houses, bougainvillea-draped stairs, and a working harbour lined with cafes and dive shops. The ancient Lycian rock tomb sits carved into the hillside right above the streets. Walkable, lively, and the base for most restaurants, boat trips, and daily errands, though busiest and priciest in peak summer.
bestFor: first-time visitors, cafe workers, harbour and old-town lovers
pros: Walk to everything, including dive shops and cafes
Lycian rock tomb and old-town character on your doorstep
cons: Loud and crowded in July and August

name: Cukurbag Peninsula
tagline: A quieter, villa-lined peninsula with sea views on both sides
description: A narrow peninsula stretching west of the harbour, lined with villas, small apartment blocks, and boutique hotels overlooking the sea on either side. Popular with longer-stay visitors and those wanting a quieter base with a car or scooter, a short ride from the town center. Fewer shops and restaurants, more residential calm and sunset views.
bestFor: longer stays, those with a scooter or car, sunset seekers
cons: Need transport for daily errands and dining

name: Kucuk Cakil & Buyuk Cakil Beach Area
tagline: Kas's pebble-beach strip just east of the harbour
description: The pebble beaches of Kucuk Cakil (small) and Buyuk Cakil (big) sit a short walk east of the harbour, backed by a promenade of beach clubs, cafes, and casual restaurants. A good base for swimmers who want the sea within steps, with easier, flatter walking than the old town's slopes, and still close enough to reach the center on foot.
bestFor: swimmers, beach-day regulars, easy walking access
pros: Flatter terrain than the old town
Still walkable to the harbour center
cons: Beach clubs get crowded and pricier in summer

name: Kalkan
tagline: A polished neighboring resort town, 25-30 minutes down the coast
description: A hillside harbour town about 25-30 minutes from Kas by dolmus or car, Kalkan is more upscale and boutique-hotel driven, with white Ottoman-Greek style buildings, fine-dining terraces, and a glossier international crowd. Many nomads base in Kas but visit Kalkan for a change of pace, a nicer dinner out, or to compare a quieter, pricier alternative base.
bestFor: day trips, special dinners, those wanting a quieter luxury base
cons: Requires a dolmus, taxi, or car to reach from Kas
